_: In Iran, since 1981, after the 1979 Islamic Revolution, the hijab has become compulsory. All women are required to wear loose-fitting clothing and a headscarf in public.

In May 2022, the Taliban made a law requiring all women to wear a burqa, which covers the entire face, or niqab, which covers the face except for the eyes. Reports vary as to the level of enforcement authorities are devoting to the law.

Saudi Arabia has one of the strictest dress codes for women in the world. All women in the country, including non-Muslim foreign visitors, are required to wear an abaya which is a loose robe-like over garment that covers the entire body except for the head, feet and hands. In …
Brunei officially implemented Sharia law in 2014. The new penal code required Muslim women to wear a headscarf covering the hair, neck and ears in public or face fines or imprisonment.
